headline: Six Infrastructure Bets That Hold Their Thesis Through the Noise
lede: A volatile session changes the price of a stock but rarely the underlying reason to own it. Six names — spanning flash storage, memory, satellite broadband, sovereign cloud, connectors, and repurposed bitcoin mines — illustrate what conviction in structural compounders actually looks like.
body:
Markets have a talent for turning durable theses into intraday soap operas. Prices gap down on macro headlines; portfolios get stress-tested against rate-cut calendars and tariff memos. Yet the physical and logical infrastructure upon which the next decade of computing, communication, and electrification will run does not pause because the Federal Reserve surprised in either direction. Six holdings — SanDisk, Micron, AST SpaceMobile, Nebius Group, TE Connectivity, and IREN — represent what one might call the **structural-compounder** framework: companies whose moat is not a product cycle but an embedded position in a layer of the economy that must be built or rebuilt regardless of short-term sentiment.

Sandisk ($SNDK) returned to public markets in February 2025 when Western Digital completed its spin-off of the flash-memory business, relisting it on the Nasdaq under the same ticker it wore before WD's 2016 acquisition. For nearly a decade, the world's most iconic NAND flash brand was buried inside a hard-drive company, its growth potential penalised by the parent's slower revenue cadence. As a standalone entity — and a pure-play in *NAND flash*, the non-volatile storage medium inside every smartphone, SSD, and data-centre storage array — Sandisk can be priced on semiconductor multiples. The AI inference boom, which demands cheap, dense, fast storage sitting below GPU clusters, has materially improved the demand outlook for high-capacity QLC (quad-level cell) NAND.

Micron ($MU) occupies the memory layer above storage: it is the only US-headquartered manufacturer of both DRAM and NAND at scale. Its recent transformation centres on *HBM — high-bandwidth memory* — a class of stacked DRAM chips mounted directly beside the processor die in AI accelerators. HBM3E, Micron's current flagship, offers roughly 30% lower power draw than competitors' equivalents and is priced at multiples of standard DDR5. The company's entire 2026 HBM capacity is sold out under binding agreements; HBM4 is sampling now, with mass production slated for late 2026. The persistent scepticism about memory cyclicality has kept Micron's forward P/E surprisingly compressed for a business posting record margins.

AST SpaceMobile ($ASTS) is attempting something genuinely novel: a constellation of very large satellites in low Earth orbit that beam broadband directly to ordinary, unmodified smartphones. No special handset, no proprietary dish. The company holds carrier agreements covering roughly three billion potential subscribers — AT&T, Verizon, Vodafone, Rakuten among them — and has $1 billion in hard commercial commitments locked in. BlueBird 6, the largest commercial communications array ever placed in LEO, reached orbit in December 2025. Continuous US service is targeted for late 2026. The thesis rests on global connectivity as a structural deficit: roughly 40% of the planet's land mass remains unserved by terrestrial mobile networks.

Nebius Group ($NBIS) is the renamed international rump of Yandex after the Russian search giant sold all of its domestic operations for $5.4 billion in 2024. Led by co-founder Arkady Volozh and headquartered in Amsterdam, the company has pivoted into **GPU cloud infrastructure** — what analysts now call a *neocloud*, a data-centre operator purpose-built for AI workloads rather than repurposed from general-purpose compute. Yandex's engineering heritage in large-scale distributed systems is a plausible differentiator. Revenue for 2025 was $529.8 million, a 479% year-on-year increase; management has guided to $3.0–3.4 billion in 2026. The sovereign-cloud angle — a European-jurisdiction GPU provider not subject to US export controls — gives it a somewhat differentiated addressable market.

TE Connectivity ($TE) is perhaps the most unglamorous name on the list, which may be the point. The company makes the connectors, sensors, and terminals that allow electricity or data to cross a physical boundary reliably — from the high-voltage harness inside an electric vehicle to the splice deep on the ocean floor. It is a toll-road on electrification: every new EV, every grid upgrade, every renewable-energy installation requires more of its components. Content-per-vehicle in 800V EV architectures runs roughly 30% above internal-combustion equivalents. In February 2025, TE announced the acquisition of Richards Manufacturing, a grid-distribution hardware maker, for $2.3 billion — signalling an expansion from vehicles into the grid itself. IREN Limited ($IREN), formerly Iris Energy, completes the basket as perhaps its most dramatic reinvention story: a bitcoin miner that recognised its scarce asset was not the cryptocurrency but the **power capacity** underneath it. The company rebranded in November 2024 and has since signed a reported $9.7 billion, five-year cloud-compute agreement with Microsoft, deploying 76,000 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs at its Childress, Texas campus on renewable power. Its first profitable fiscal year — net income of $86.9 million on $501 million in revenue for 2025 — arrived just as the AI infrastructure land-grab intensified. The thesis is that power, not silicon, is the binding constraint in the AI build-out, and that IREN locked in gigawatts before the market fully priced that scarcity.

concepts.definition: A company whose competitive position is tied to a secular, multi-year demand shift in the underlying economy rather than a product cycle or macro tailwind. The idea is that the thesis survives — and often strengthens — through short-term price volatility, because the structural need being addressed does not go away.

A type of non-volatile semiconductor storage that retains data without power. It is the medium inside solid-state drives, USB sticks, and smartphone storage. 'NAND' refers to the logic gate architecture used; 'flash' refers to the ability to erase and rewrite data in large blocks. QLC (quad-level cell) NAND stores four bits per cell, maximising density at some cost to write endurance.

A class of DRAM (dynamic random-access memory) in which multiple memory dies are stacked vertically and connected through the silicon itself via 'through-silicon vias,' then placed directly beside a processor. The result is dramatically higher data-transfer bandwidth than standard DRAM at lower power. HBM is mandatory in high-end AI training and inference accelerators.

A data-centre operator built specifically to serve AI and machine-learning workloads, typically offering GPU compute on a bare-metal or cloud basis. Neoclouds differ from hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) in that they specialise in GPU density and AI-specific networking rather than general-purpose compute services.

The orbital band roughly 200–2,000 kilometres above Earth's surface. Satellites in LEO complete an orbit in roughly 90 minutes and, because of the lower altitude, impose far less signal latency than traditional geostationary satellites at 36,000 km. Lower latency makes LEO suitable for broadband internet delivery.

fact_check: Revenue and financial figures for Micron, Nebius, and IREN are drawn from reported earnings as summarised in financial media through early 2026; the Nebius-Meta deal figure of $2.7 billion and the IREN-Microsoft figure of $9.7 billion were reported in financial media but had not been independently confirmed in primary filings as of the research date — treat these as reported, not verified. The SNDK price appreciation figures (from ~$38.50 at spinoff to hundreds of dollars) appear in multiple sources but were not cross-referenced against exchange data. The '40% of land mass unserved' connectivity figure is a widely cited industry estimate; the precise sourcing varies.
